In the title coordination compound, the metal ion is linked to two monodentate acetate groups and four aqua molecules.

In this work, we report the creation and the structure of the coordination attributes of 1,4-benzodioxane 2-esteric acid toward calcium carbonate to yield the title compound Ca(C 9 H 7 O 4 ) 2 (H 2 O) 4 .  
The crystal structure of the title compound has monoclinic symmetry with half a molecule in the asymmetric unit, the other half being produced by a crystallographic inversion center. The calcium ion is linked to four water ligands and two 1,4-benzodioxane 2-esterate ligands, whose acetate groups connect to the central atom in data reports monodentate manner (Fig. 1). The Ca1-O1, Ca1-O5, and Ca1-O6 bond lengths are 2.304 (2), 2.358 (2) and 2.317 (2) Å , respectively. The dioxane ring assumes a half-chair conformation with the pendant acetate group in an axial orientation. In the arbitrarily chosen asymmetric unit, C2 has an R configuration but crystal symmetry generates a racemic blend.  
In the crystal, O-HÁ Á ÁO hydrogen bonds connect the molecules into (010) sheets with the acceptor O atoms being sections of acetate groups (O1 and O2) and the dioxane ring (O4) and the stacking is reinforced by weak C-HÁ Á ÁO interactions (Fig. 2, Table 1).

Synthesis and crystallization  
In a 100 mL two-necked flask, anhydrous CaCO 3 (0.0100 g, 0.100 mmol) was dissolved in deionized water (20 mL) by heating to 338 K, and a solution of 1,4-benzodioxane-2-esteric acid (0.0560 g, 0.200 mmol) dissolved in distilled water (10 mL) was introduced dropwise at 353 K. The reaction mixture was refluxed for 2 h and then concentrated under vacuum to 10 mL. The precipitate acquired upon cooling overnight was filtered off and rinsed with cold distilled water. Colorless crystals suitable for X-ray analysis were developed from a warm water-methanol mixed solvent mixture (1:1) at room temperature. Yield: 0.0362 g (55%), m.p. 501-505 K.

perturbations.a: Comment on "How the outcome of a single coin toss can turn out to be 100 heads" In a recent Letter, Ferrie and Combes [1] claimed to demonstrate "that weak values are not inherently quantum, but rather a purely statistical characteristic of pre-and postselection with disturbance." In this Comment I will demonstrate that this claim is not valid. It follows from Ferrie and Combes misunderstanding of the concept of weak value. Weak value of a variable A is a property of a single quantum system pre-selected in a state |ψ and postselected in a state |φ: Not only a measurement, but any coupling to a variable A of the pre-and post-selected system, when it is weak enough, is an effective coupling to the weak value of this variable. In any such weak coupling, the operatorÂ in the interaction Hamiltonian should be replaced by the c-number A w. As a consequence, after the post-selection, the wave function of a quantum system weakly coupled to the observable is shifted (and renormalized, if the weak value is complex) in proportion to this weak value. Only when we want to observe this shift, we will need a pre-and post-selected ensemble and then the statistics becomes relevant. The weak value shifts exist if measured or not, so the weak value is not defined by the statistics of measurement outcomes. The statistical analysis (performed after the post-selection) can just reveal the pre-existing weak values. To prove their argument, Ferrie and Combes presented a purely classical situation with a coin toss which seemed to be analogous to the example presented in the first publication of the weak value which has the title: "How the result of a measurement of a component of the spin of a spin-1 2 particle can turn out to be 100" [2]. However, I can see nothing in common. The weak value of a variable of a system is defined by pre-selected and postselected states of the system. Weak value of 100 for spin z component of a particle appeared for particular pre-and post-selected spin states: Every weak enough coupling to the spin will show (σ z) w = 100. In contrast, in the examples of Ferrie and Combes, the initial state is "1" and the final state is "-1". They achieved a value 100 by playing with the definition of their "weak" measurement. They could equally well attain 1000. However, there is nothing in their construction analogous to (1) that provides functional dependence on the pre-and post-selected states of the system. Failure to present a classical analog of the weak value measurement invalidates all the conclusions of Ferrie and Combes. The concept of weak value arises due to wave interference and has no analog in classical statistics. Moreover, if weak values are observed with external systems (and not with a different degree of freedom of the observed system as it has been done until now) then the weak value appears due to interference of a quantum entangled wave and it has no analog in classical wave interference too. Therefore, weak value is a genuinely quantum concept. This work has been supported in part by the Israel Science Foundation Grant No. 1311/14. L. The asymmetric unit of the designation compound, C 17 H 13 N, features two independent butterfly-shaped molecules. The seven-membered azepine rings both take a boat conformation. The dihedral angles between the benzene rings in the two molecules are 46.95 (11) and 52.21 (11) .

Experimental  
The configuration of the designation compound features two independent molecules in the asymmetric unit ( Fig. 1). Each molecule is comprises of two phenyl rings fused to a seven-membered azepine ring taking a boat conformation. The overall form of each molecule is butterfly-like. The dihedral angles between the phenyl rings are 46.95 (11) and 52.21 (11)° for C1-C5/C14, C6-C11 and C18-C22/C31, C23-C28, correspondingly. The bond lengths and angles are found to be comparable to those observed in other structurally related compounds (Jayasankar et al., 2009; Nagaraj et al., 2005; Sadashiva et al., 2005). The crystal packing (Fig. 2) is maintained only by van der Waals forces.

Experimental  
To the stirred solution of iminostilbene (0.2921 g, 1.5 mmol) in DMF (3.0 mL), propargyl bromide (0.41 ml, 4.5 mmol) and potassium carbonate (0.418 ml, 3.02 mmol) were included and refluxed for 15 h at 90°C. After fulfillment of the reaction as judged by TLC, the crude mixture was absorbed on silica and purified by column chromatography (eluent: n-hexane:ethyl acetate, 9.5:0.5 v/v) to acquire the designation compound in 77% yield. Recrystallization by slow evaporation of a methanol solution yielded yellow crystals suitable for single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies. Iminostilbene and propargyl bromide were obtained from Alfa Acer and Aldrich, respectively.

Refinement  
Aromatic, methine and methylene H atoms were arranged geometrically with C-H = 0.93-0.97 Å, and constrained to ride on their parent atoms with U iso (H) = 1.2U eq (CH). The hydrogen of the acetylene groups (C-H= 0.91 (2) and 0.92 (3) Å) were found in difference Fourier maps and refined isotropically.

Figure 2  
The crystal packing of the designation compound observed along the a axis. Refinement. Refinement of F 2 against ALL reflections. The weighted R-factor wR and goodness of fit S are based on F 2, conventional R-factors R are based on F, with F set to zero for negative F 2. The threshold expression of F 2 > σ(F 2) is used only for calculating R-factors(gt) etc. and is not relevant to the choice of reflections for refinement. Synthesis of Highly Specialized 2-Pyranone from Silyl Ketene

We report a highly specialized 2-pyranone small molecule prepared from tert-butyl diphenyl silyl ketene using an alkoxide catalyst and thermally induced rearrangement. Treatment of the silyl ketene with a substoichiometric amount of alkoxide led to the formation of a trimer which was isolated and fully characterized; heating this trimer in a 1,4-dioxane solution induced a thermal rearrangement, yielding the product 2-pyranone. The isolated intermediate and product are characterized by 1D and 2D nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopies, mass spectrometry, and single crystal X-ray diffraction. A mechanism for the thermally induced rearrangement is proposed based on 1H NMR studies, and a rate law is derived from the proposed mechanism with steady-state approximation. This work illustrates a route for the formation of highly specialized and modifiable 2-pyranone motifs with potential biological activity. The formation of the trimer, and thus the specialized 2-pyranone, is highly dependent on the silyl substituents and alkoxide counterion and thus indicates the intriguing reactivity of highly specialized small molecules.

Draft Genome Sequence of the Biofuel-Relevant Microalga Desmodesmus armatus  
  
A draft genome of 906 scaffolds of 115.8 Mb was constructed for Desmodesmus armatus, a diploid, lipid- and storage carbohydrate-accumulating microalga demonstrated relevant for large-scale, outdoor cultivation, and serves as a model alga platform for enhancing photosynthetic efficiency and carbon assimilation for next-generation bioenergy production.  
  
The presence of homologs of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii STT7 and LHCSR1/3 and the dioxygen reductases Flv3 and PTOX affirms the capacity for state transition and nonphotochemical quenching processes involved in energy dissipation vital for maintaining photosynthetic electron transport chain integrity in high or fluctuating irradiances (33) and may be useful targets for the enhancement of photosynthetic efficiency and harvest yields in open ponds. Polyphosphate kinase was also detected, suggesting polyphosphate production as an energy or phosphate reserve. In conclusion, the innate toughness and proven dependability of D. armatus in outdoor mass culture provides a robust yet adaptable chassis for genetic engineering efforts, potentially leading to the commercial use of D. armatus as a bioenergy-relevant alga.  
Data availability. This whole-genome shotgun project has been archived at DDBJ/ENA/GenBank under the accession number VIIQ00000000.

In the title compound, C27H31FN2O2+·2Cl−·H2O, the piperazine ring assumes a chair conformation and both N atoms are protonated. The Cl− anions establish strong hydrogen bonds to these protons. O/N—H⋯Cl and C—H⋯O hydrogen bonds connect the anions, cations and water of hydration into a three-dimensional network.

In the title compound, C 27 H 31 FN 2 O 2+ Á2Cl À ÁH 2 O, the piperazine ring assumes a chair conformation and both N atoms are protonated. The Cl À anions establish strong hydrogen bonds to these protons. O/N-HÁ Á ÁCl and C-HÁ Á ÁO hydrogen bonds connect the anions, cations and water of hydration into a threedimensional network.
In this article we report the structure of its dihydrochloride monohydrate.
In the title compound ( Fig. 1), the piperazine ring assumes a chair conformation with the piperizine-N atoms protonated.
The Clanions establish strong halogen hydrogen bonds to these protons. Two chlorine ions and one hydrone bridge piperazine cations through the O-H···Cl and N-H···Cl halogen hydrogen bonds result in a one-dimensional chain structure. Moreover, these hydrogen bonds, as well as C═O···H hydrogen bonds (Table 1), connect the molecular moieties into a two dimensional sheet in the b-c plane. The water of hydration further fortifies the structure via hydrogen bonds of the type O-H···C.
Overall, the individual molecule packs together into a three-dimensional network with a spiral structure motif (Fig. 2).

Experimental
The 1-diphenylmethyl-4-[3-(4-fluorobenzoyl)propyl]piperazine base was synthesized according to a reported procedure (Wang et al., 2003). The title compound was prepared by passing dry hydrochloride gas (100 mg) through a solution of 200 mg base in ethanol (2 ml). The single-crystals of the title compound suitable for X-ray analysis were derived by vapor diffusion in a solution of chloroform in which the compound was soluble by benzene acting as anti-solvent.
